text:
Ellen: proposal: add a tenant-aware onboarding sweep that evaluates a candidate model across representative tenant workloads before a global rollout. rationale: some regressions only show up under downstream prompt mixes or tenant-specific temperature settings.
Tao: interesting. how is this different from SHADOW/ensemble?
Ellen: SHADOW is generic replay and ensemble compares to prod in-the-wild. tenant-sweep runs a short, bounded battery of target-tenant traces (sanitized), plus a tiny per-tenant cost/latency profile. think of it as a targeted smoke+profiling for top N tenants.
Priya: data privacy concerns: we need strict sanitization and tenancy consent. can't just mirror customer prompts.
Ellen: yes — only tenants who opt-in (or internal test tenants) get swept. data gets redacted client-side and runs in isolated VPC test workers. audit log for each run.
Morgan: how big is the sweep? cost? schedule?
Ellen: plan: top-20 tenants by QPS, 200 requests each sampled from recent anonymized traces, run in parallel on dedicated small GPUs. expected cost ~2 GPU-hours per full sweep. We can do nightly for critical major bumps, or on-demand for canaries.
Tao: metrics to capture? I want latency distribution, embedding-drift vs baseline, tokenization diffs, and per-intent quality deltas. Also rack memory/kv-cache divergence.
Priya: add per-tenant sensitivity: some tenants are creative (high variance), so thresholds should be per-tenant and learned from baseline history. dev tenants can be permissive.
Morgan: rollout policy integration? block on tenant-sweep fail? that could be noisy.
Ellen: default policy: tenant-sweep is advisory for non-prod tenants and mandatory for tenants with strict SLAs (we'll have a tenant flag in Console). For mandatory tenants, any tier-1 regression (latency tail + correctness drop > threshold) blocks global promotion until triage.
Tao: how to avoid gaming by submitters (tuning prompts to pass)?
Ellen: deterministic invariants still checked earlier (tokenizer hash, kv layout). tenant-sweep focuses on behavioral drift; we store the baseline per-tenant model snapshot for comparison and require reproducible sampling. Also delta thresholds are set conservatively and ownership assigned.
Priya: owners? infra? privacy?
Ellen: eng-ml owns sweep infra; product-ops owns tenant-sensitivity defaults and takes final escalation; legal signs off on redaction and tenant opt-in wording. Eng-sre will help size quotas.
Morgan: UX: Console should show per-tenant sweep status: SWEEP_OK / SWEEP_WARN / SWEEP_FAIL and a short link to a per-tenant summary with top failing intents and sample anonymized inputs. Also allow tenants to opt-out per-team.
Tao: action items: 1) Ellen+Tao draft sweep spec (sampling, anonymization, thresholds), 2) Priya define tenant-sensitivity heuristics, 3) Morgan wire Console flags and per-tenant state, 4) eng-sre quota estimate and opt-in controls.
